summary: Candidate research identifies two complementary national resources: an official catalog for dataset metadata and harvest history, and a provenance specification for representing source-to-assertion lineage. They are governance aids, not New Brunswick hospital measurements; discovery does not establish that any source was acquired or approved for simulation use.

sources.title: Data.gov Catalog API and user guide
sources.geography: U.S. federal catalog, with some state/local entries when their metadata is harvested
sources.period: Continuously updated catalog; record metadata includes modified and metadata-last-checked dates, and harvest records provide source and transformed payloads
sources.grain: Dataset catalog entry or harvest record; not hospital-level clinical or operational records
useful_fields: license and access level when supplied
observed_facts: The official guide documents a public JSON API that requires no authentication, including dataset search and harvest-record retrieval.
Dataset pages may expose publisher-provided license and access information, metadata dates, and distribution links; these fields can be absent.
The API can support bounded discovery of official metadata records, but the catalog itself is not evidence that a listed distribution has been downloaded or validated.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For a bounded metadata audit, query the documented search endpoint for the exact CMS, CDC, NPPES, NJ, and hospital source titles already catalogued; retain only exact matching records and distribution URLs. For each selected result, retrieve its harvest record and transformed payload using the guide's documented routes; save query parameters, retrieval time, response hash, source/record identifier, and any missing license or access fields. Do not infer rights from catalog inclusion.
limitations: The inspected documentation describes routes and fields but does not verify the proposed example package_search URL as a data endpoint; confirm the current API documentation before collection.
Catalog metadata may be incomplete, harvested on a schedule, or describe resources whose publisher terms differ; verify each original publisher's terms and file/version independently.
No local New Brunswick or Middlesex County hospital dataset was identified or acquired through this catalog review.
Not a source of clinical approval, facility applicability, or local quantitative estimates.

sources.title: PROV Model Primer
sources.geography: International technical specification; applicable as an external modeling reference
sources.period: Published 2013; specification reference, with current status to be checked against W3C publications
sources.grain: Provenance statements linking entities, activities, agents, usage, generation, derivation, and time
useful_fields: assertion identity and review status as project-specific extensions
observed_facts: The primer describes PROV as a model for representing entities, processes, and agents involved in producing data or other objects.
It explains provenance uses including tracing collection and transformation processes, evaluating rights and trust, and reproducing generation steps.
The opened page identifies the primer as a W3C Working Group Note and links to the PROV ontology and data model recommendations.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the public primer and linked normative PROV-DM/PROV-O documents to map each source release, record or assertion, transformation, and review decision into an auditable lineage graph. Preserve project-specific fields for retrieval time, release time, valid time, rights evidence, scope, epistemic status, and independent review; validate those extensions against the applicable project schema.
limitations: This is a standard/reference document, not an empirical dataset, and supplies no hospital-specific records or legal determination of reuse rights.
The opened primer is dated and states that other publications may supersede it; check current W3C status before treating it as the normative version.
PROV does not itself supply clinical approval criteria or decide whether a derived assertion is suitable for simulation.

missing_inputs: No new, directly measured public quantitative dataset specific to RWJUH CCN310038, Saint Peter's CCN310070, or Middlesex County was verified in this bounded search.

No inspected source supplied exact local release-level lineage or review-decision records for the existing 19 source IDs; the current catalogs and upstream source snapshots must be audited separately.
No verified direct downloadable hospital-specific provenance or data-rights endpoint was found.
simulation_use: Use the Data.gov API as an optional bounded discovery and metadata-history aid for federal and harvested public datasets, and use PROV concepts to represent source-release → record/assertion → transformation → review lineage. Keep provenance completeness and rights status as explicit governance fields; unknown rights block redistribution, and acquisition does not imply clinical approval. Neither candidate calibrates hospital behavior or local population and encounter quantities.
limitations: This output is candidate research for independent verification; no dataset was acquired.
Only two searches and three primary pages were inspected. No local estimate, source version, or endpoint is inferred beyond what was observed.
The Data.gov example API URL is a documented service pattern, not a verified direct dataset/download URL; consult the current API documentation before using it.
Public catalog metadata and an external provenance model do not establish source rights, site applicability, or simulation readiness.
